**The on-screen keyboard lost its frames.** Every key cell and every action button was drawn with a white hairline
box, and the global filter brightened the button art until it glared. The keyboard is now what it should have been
from the start: a black slab with square keys, no borders, and glyphs that keep their own contrast.

**The Library tab you selected can finally be read.** The white pill behind the active tab made its own label
invisible, because Steam colours the text inside it. The pill is gone: the selected tab is now marked with a hairline
underline and brighter text, the same way the rest of the interface marks what is active.

**A red accent, if you want one.** The panel has a new **Red accents** switch. It turns the focus rings, the borders
and the status dots red instead of white, so the whole interface can read as a single warning colour without
changing a single line of Steam's behaviour.

**Everything else stayed as it was.** The Home screen, the downloads page, the startup movie, the compatibility
badges and the custom Home keep the treatment they had in 1.7.1, and the plugin still only changes how Steam looks,
never how it works.

**Install / update:** grab `VoidDeck-v1.8.0.zip` from the [v1.8.0 release](https://github.com/endoflineservice/VoidDeck/releases/tag/v1.8.0), or press **Update now** in the Void Deck panel.
